title: Touch target size and focus rings
when: Controls are hard to tap on phones or keyboard focus is invisible, and the user wants comfortable, visible targets.
inputs: surface colors where focus must show
prompt:
Goal: Every control at least 44 by 44 px (WCAG 2.2 minimum 24 px with spacing) and a focus ring visible on any background.
Steps:
1. Find small targets: icon buttons, dense list links, checkboxes, close buttons, pagination.
2. Grow the hit area, not the look: padding with min-width and min-height 44px, or a ::before with inset: -10px on a position: relative control.
3. Keep at least 8 px between adjacent targets so a thumb hits one.
4. Focus: :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--color-focus); outline-offset: 2px }; never remove outline without a replacement.
5. Choose a focus color with 3 to 1 against both control and page, or a two tone ring (outline plus a box-shadow in the background color).
6. Enlarge checkboxes and radios with inline-size: 1.25rem and accent-color, and make the whole label clickable.
Quality bar:
- Focus ring visible on light, dark and accent surfaces.
- No target under 24 px without 24 px of spacing.
- Focused anchors are not hidden under a sticky header (scroll-margin-top).
Pitfalls:
- outline: none in a reset.
- Hit areas overlapping neighbors.
- Focus styles applied only on :hover.
Verify:
- [ ] A :focus-visible rule covers interactive elements.
- [ ] Icon buttons measure at least 44 px.
- [ ] Adjacent targets keep 8 px.
- [ ] scroll-margin-top set under a sticky header.
Output: Target size and focus rules in style.css.

examples.input: os botoes de icone sao dificeis de tocar no celular
examples.output: icon buttons min 44px with padding, 3px focus ring with 2px offset, 8px gap between controls
